title: INNOVATIVE MECHANICAL BEARING PULLER REMOVAL
abstract: This study focused on the development and evaluation of an Innovative Mechanical Bearing Puller Removal intended for automotive servicing applications, particularly in removing bearings from starter motors and similar mechanical components. The study aimed to provide a practical, low-cost, and efficient alternative to commercially available bearing pullers by utilizing locally available materials and simple fabrication techniques. Specifically, the study evaluated the improvised tool in terms of ease of use, efficiency, safety, accuracy, and durability. The study employed a quantitative descriptive-developmental research design. Fifty (50) Automotive Technology students from Cebu Technological University-Daanbantayan Campus served as respondents during the Academic Year 2025-2026. Data were gathered using a researcher-made questionnaire and observation checklist. Statistical tools such as frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and ranking were used to analyze the gathered data. Findings revealed that the improvised bearing puller obtained "Strongly Agree" ratings in all evaluation criteria. The respondents positively evaluated the tool in terms of ease of use (4.45), efficiency (4.36), safety (4.37), accuracy (4.35), durability (4.44), and overall evaluation (4.54). The results indicate that the improvised bearing puller is effective, reliable, safe, and can serve as a practical alternative to commercial bearing pullers. The study concluded that locally fabricated tools can successfully address mechanical maintenance needs while promoting innovation, resourcefulness, and practical learning among students and technicians.

title: IMPROVISED BRAKE PISTON PRESSER
abstract:
The improvised Brake Piston Presser is a simple and cost-effective tool designed to assist in compressing brake caliper pistons during vehicle brake maintenance. This study aimed to develop an alternative piston pressing devise using locally available and affordable materials without compromising functionality and safety. The improvised tool was created to provide an accessible solution for mechanics, automotive students, and vehicle owners who may not have access to expensive commercial brake piston compressors.
The device was tested for durability, ease of use, efficiency, and effectiveness in pressing brake pistons and brake pad replacement procedures. Results showed that the improvised brake piston presser was capable of performing the intended function effectively while reducing maintenance time and effort. Additionally, the tool demonstrated practicality, portability, and affordability compared to commercially available equipment.
The study concludes that the improvised brake piston presser can serve as a reliable alternative tool for basic automotive brake servicing. It is recommended for educational workshops, small automotive repair shops, and personal vehicle maintenance applications.

title: TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION FOR IMPROVISED BATTERY POWERED ENGINE GENERATOR
abstract:
This research focuses on the technology adoption and development of an improvised Battery-Powered Engine Generator designed to provide an alternative source of electricity during emergency situations such as power outages caused by typhoons, earthquakes, and other calamities. The project utilizes a small motorcycle engine integrated with essential components such as a CDI, regulator, battery, and an added inverter to convert stored electrical energy into a usable 220-volt AC output. A compact and portable chassis was also designed to allow easy mobility and practical use in different locations.
Using a descriptive research method and evaluation from first-year college student respondents, the study assessed the system in terms of functionality, efficiency, safety, portability, and economic feasibility. The results indicate that the improvised generator effectively provides stable electrical output suitable for basic emergency applications. The respondents rated the system as easy to operate, cost-efficient, and practical compared to conventional generator sets. The portable design further enhanced usability, particularly during emergency situations where quick deployment is necessary.
The study concludes that the improvised battery-powered engine generator is a practical and innovative solution for emergency power needs and an effective instructional tool for introductory engineering and technology courses. It highlights the importance of adopting simple and accessible technologies to address real-world energy challenges. Further testing, design improvement, and academic integration are recommended for future development.
